page.layout: Top: running head "CAP. VIII. PROBL. I." with page number 143 at the top right. Then a block of numbered theses 4 to 21 in italic, one column at full width. Below it, centred: "IN CAPVT OCTAVVM.", "PROBLEMA I.", and an italic question. Then one column of running text with notes in the right margin, and the section numbers I., II:, III. beside the last lines in the right margin.

l.i: 4 Estque vel rei, vel signi.
5 Veritas rei est congruentia illius, cum sua natura.
6 Estque vel incomplexa, vel complexa.
7 Veritas incomplexa est, per quam ens incomplexum dicitur
verum.
8 Estque vel prima, vel à prima orta.
9 Veritas prima est, quæ ab æterno in ipso Deo creatore existit.
10 Veritas à prima orta est, quæ in ipsis creaturis existit.
11 Veritas complexa est, per quam ens complexum dicitur
verum.
12 Utraque veritas tam incomplexa, quam complexa, vel
est necessaria, vel contingens.
13 Veritas necessaria est, per quam ens necessario est verum;
sive simpliciter, sive secundum quid.
14 Veritas contingens est, per quam ens contingenter est verum.
15 Sic de veritate rei. Sequitur veritas signi, quæ est
congruentia illius, cum re signata.
16 Eius species sunt veritas conceptus, & vocis.
17 Veritas conceptus, est conformitas illius cum re, quam
repræsentat.
18 Veritas vocis, est congruentia illius cum re, quam significat.
19 Estque vel sermonis vel scriptura; quorum prior est per
quam sermo. posterior, per quam scriptura dicitur vera.
20 Porro falsitas est incongruentia entis cum suo archetypo.
21 Estque similiter vel rei, vel signi; vel incomplexa vel
complexa; vel necessaria vel contingens.
An vox veritatis semper uno & eodem modo
usurpetur?

main_text.l: IN vestibulo doctrinæ de veritate ante omnia confi-der-
anda[?] est ipsa vox veritatis: ac cum illa sit ambigua,
excutienda sunt diuersa illius significata, vt sciatur, in qua
significatione deinceps sit accipienda, ne impru-
dentes in errorem incidamus. Sciendum igitur est voca-
bulum veritatis quandoque sumi pro veracitate quæ est
virtus moralis, per quam sermo naturæ intelligentis ita

page.notes:
The page number "143" is clear but the first digit could be read as I; I read it as 143. The word "confi-deranda" is printed with a line-end hyphen and the reading is doubtful; the sense suggests "consi-deranda", so it is marked [?]. The marginal note "Diuersa sign." is worn at the edge; the reading of the abbreviation is as printed. Theses 4 to 21 are numbered in the printed text and are kept as

. The printed page number may be partly obscured at the top right. No catchword, signature or other bottom furniture is visible. The bottom of the page is faint, but the last line ends with "ita", which continues on the next page.
